description:
Found s361 while probing perl's t/comp/proto.t trailing-`;` list-op family (the #153 step-3b arity work). Pre-existing.

  sub u3(;$;) { $_[0]+1 }
  print "A3=", (u3 0 || 5), "\n";     # perl: A3=6
  print "done\n";                     # PCL:  only "done" — the A3 line is GONE

Emitted CL for the print statement is literally:
  (progn ;; PARSE ERROR: Bug. Fell through. Missing case: [
   nil)

So the statement is replaced by nil and execution continues — the #138 family (silently deleted statement), and the loudest possible clue is already in the output as a comment nobody reads. Two things worth separating:
 (a) the parse gap itself: `(;$;)` (leading AND trailing `;`) is a legal prototype; PCL's `_parse_old_prototype` handles it, so the failure is further along — likely the call site's arg derivation. `($;)` and `(_;)` (the other two spellings in t/comp/proto.t) both work, so this is the leading-`;` variant only.
 (b) RULE-12 QUESTION: a "PARSE ERROR … Missing case" that lowers to `nil` is exactly the value-producing swallow the s329 boundary says must DIE (the statement's value IS consumed — it is a print argument). Whether the fall-through should die or announce belongs with whoever owns the PARSE-ERROR path, not with this one prototype.

Cheap discriminating measurement, if picked up: transpile `sub u3(;$;){} u3 0;` and `sub u3(;$;){} u3(0);` — the paren form should tell whether the gap is in the prototype record or in the paren-less arg derivation.</description>
</invoke>
